clusters.pick_reason: Per its changeset, #2763's fix covers both halves of the bug: it caps the initial timer with Math.min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout) for the no-progress case, and re-arms progress-triggered resets against the remaining maxTotalTimeout budget (raising 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' when the cap is hit) — the same reset code path #2817 touches. #2817's diff only adds `info.startTime = Date.now()` before re-arming with the full per-request `info.timeout`, plus a comment-only test change; it does not clamp the reset delay to the remaining maxTotalTimeout budget, so a call that keeps receiving progress notifications could still run past maxTotalTimeout. #2763 also ships a `.changeset/*.md` entry for all three affected packages (core-internal, client, server) as this repo's changeset check requires; #2817's diff contains no changeset file.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same close() logic in packages/server/src/server/streamableHttp.ts (same base commit c0f48560a2) to settle parked JSON-response-mode POSTs on transport close, so they'd directly conflict if both merged. #2600 is the superset fix: in addition to settling parked JSON-mode responses, it also clears _requestToStreamMapping (which #2692's description doesn't address) and fixes a distinct race where send() suspended inside eventStore.storeEvent() across a close() call resumes against a retired correlation, leaking both the response and its correlation for the process lifetime. #2692 only covers the response-settling half of the same problem with a different error payload (-32000 'Connection closed' vs #2600's 404 'Session not found').

members.title: fix(server): retire in-flight request state when the streamable HTTP transport closes
members.author: rxits
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves in-flight JSON-response-mode POST requests unsettled: handleRequest()'s returned Promise<Response> is only resolved by send(), and close() tears down the stream mapping without resolving it, so the HTTP request hangs until the platform's own socket/timeout fires instead of getting an immediate response. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Per its changeset, #2763's fix covers both halves of the bug: it caps the initial timer with Math.min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout) for the no-progress case, and re-arms progress-triggered resets against the remaining maxTotalTimeout budget (raising 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' when the cap is hit) — the same reset code path #2817 touches. #2817's diff only adds `info.startTime = Date.now()` before re-arming with the full per-request `info.timeout`, plus a comment-only test change; it does not clamp the reset delay to the remaining maxTotalTimeout budget, so a call that keeps receiving progress notifications could still run past maxTotalTimeout. #2763 also ships a `.changeset/*.md` entry for all three affected packages (core-internal, client, server) as this repo's changeset check requires; #2817's diff contains no changeset file.
